verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Vercel Sandbox runs untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs, explicitly so that AI agent output can run without exposing production systems. Supporting capabilities include per-agent Linux users, timeouts and an SDK/CLI for running commands. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the isolation guarantees, documented detail on isolation boundaries such as network egress controls.

support.subject: As a developer, I can execute untrusted, AI-generated code without risking my own infrastructure

citations.quote: Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs.
Execute untrusted code safely: Run AI agent output, user uploads, or third-party scripts without exposing your production systems.
Test in isolation: Preview how user-submitted or agent-generated code behaves in a self-contained environment with access to logs, file edits, and live previews.
